misconceptions.description: Treating a cosmetic change as the operational mechanism of a learning principle
misconceptions.trigger: feature column describes a color, font, or layout polish and claims it satisfies signaling or coherence
misconceptions.feedback: Show how the feature changes what the learner processes, not how it looks. Signaling directs attention to essential material; decoration does not.

misconceptions.description: Building a feature first and then attaching a principle that sounds like it justifies the choice
misconceptions.trigger: argument runs feature to principle rather than principle and demand to feature
misconceptions.feedback: Run the trace from the principle and the demand it addresses to the feature. Do not retrofit a principle onto a feature you already chose.

misconceptions.description: Accepting AI-attached principle labels without checking the feature's actual mechanism
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps a mapping because the AI cited a real principle name
misconceptions.feedback: Audit each AI mapping against the principle's real definition. A correct principle name does not prove the feature operationalizes it.

misconceptions.description: Mapping a single feature to many principles to look thorough, hiding the absence of a controlling principle
misconceptions.trigger: every feature cites three or more principles with no controlling one named
misconceptions.feedback: Name the controlling principle and the demand it addresses. List secondary principles only if the feature was actually designed from them.
